h: Seabird Cliffs and Coast Paths Near Filey
p: Birds are the stars at the park, so it's well worth keeping the feathered theme going along the coast. A short drive south, RSPB Bempton Cliffs near Bridlington has towering chalk cliffs that teem with seabirds from spring into summer, including gannets, kittiwakes, guillemots and, if you're lucky, puffins. The viewing platforms put you right above the action, and the noise alone is unforgettable.

Closer to home, Filey Dams is a small nature reserve on the edge of town run by the Yorkshire Wildlife Trust, with hides overlooking wetland pools that attract waders and ducks. It's quiet, free and great for introducing kids to birdwatching after they've seen the more exotic species at the park.

Filey Brigg also marks a meeting of two long-distance walks: the Cleveland Way and the Yorkshire Wolds Way both finish at Filey, so the cliff-top paths are well kept and great for a stroll with views back over the bay.

In town, the Crescent Gardens above the beach are lovely for a sit-down, and down at the Coble Landing you'll see the traditional fishing boats pulled up on the slipway, with cafés and amusements nearby. Hunmanby Gap, just south of town, has a quieter stretch of sand for days when the main beach is busy. A day of birds in the park and seabirds on the cliffs makes for a memorable Yorkshire coast outing.
